headline: All majors above the 200-day line but momentum rolling over; whales pulling coins cold while stablecoins sit flat and funding splits by asset.
paragraphs: The regime is intact: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB all sit above their 200-day simple moving averages. Ethereum and Solana sport golden crosses, a bullish alignment of the 50 and 200-day lines. But the tape shows fatigue. Every major asset is down on the day, with Bitcoin at -1.83 percent, Ethereum at -2.05 percent, and Solana at -2.02 percent. RSI readings across the board tell the story: Bitcoin at 66.9, Ethereum at 62.7, Solana at 63.2, BNB at 69.4. These are not yet overbought, but they are in the upper half of the range, signaling momentum that has spent itself. The problem is clearer in the MACD: not one major asset has MACD above its signal line. Across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, and the rest, the momentum indicator has turned bearish, and momentum is diverging downward even as price clings to the 200-day support. This is the classic setup for a rest, or worse.

The distance from the 12-month high compounds the fragility. Bitcoin sits 36 percent below its 12-month peak of $124,740. Ethereum is 47.8 percent underwater, Solana 58.9 percent, XRP 55.1 percent, and worst of all, Doge is 70.7 percent and ADA 77.2 percent away from their highs. These are not young rallies. The 30-day realized volatility for XRP stands at 87.8 percent and for ADA at 83 percent, the highest in the cohort. Doge and ADA sit below their 200-day lines entirely, the only two majors to fall through. The longer-term trend is not broken, but the shorter-term pulse is weakening, and the largest drawdowns are in assets that got the most speculative air.

Positioning in the derivatives markets reveals a key bifurcation. Bitcoin funding on OKX is negative: -0.0024 percent over the last 8 hours, or -2.6 percent annualized. Shorts are being paid to stay short. But Ethereum is positive: 0.0036 percent on the 8-hour, 4.0 percent annualized. Solana swings hard negative at -0.0096 percent and -10.6 percent annualized, the deepest negative in the set, signaling heavy long positioning that is now crowded and expensive to hold. XRP funds positive at 0.0073 percent (8.0 percent annualized), Doge at 0.0099 percent (10.9 percent annualized). The long-to-short ratio diverges just as violently: Bitcoin is nearly flat at 1.06 to 1, but Solana sits at 1.95 to 1, XRP at 2.34 to 1, and Doge at 4.12 to 1. These are positions crowded in one direction. Open interest for Bitcoin stands at $2.2 billion, Ethereum at $1.47 billion, Solana at $287 million. Over the last 5 to 9 hours, liquidations have hit mostly longs: Solana long liquidations totaled $184,143 against $74,447 in shorts; XRP longs took $713,450 versus $35,436 in shorts; Doge longs liquidated $377,360 against $32,774 in shorts. Crowded positioning is beginning to unwind.

The flow picture is mixed and tensioned. Over the last 48 hours, whales moved $1.63 million net off exchanges, the first retreat from a three-week cycle of movement onto exchanges: the week ending August 28 saw $1.065 billion move onto exchanges, but the week ending September 4 reversed to $670 million moving off. Bitcoin alone moved $53.5 million off exchanges in the 48-hour window, but this masks a deeper split: $465 million in Bitcoin left cold storage and moved off exchanges, while $412 million came onto exchanges from holders, creating tension. Ethereum flipped: $51.8 million moved onto exchanges over the same period. The ETF flows show inflows on the latest session of September 3: Bitcoin took in $730.8 million on the day and $610.2 million over the last five sessions; Ethereum took in $141.4 million on the day but only $291.5 million over five sessions, meaning inflows are decelerating. Bitcoin flows have been positive for 2 same-direction days; Ethereum for only 1. Stablecoin float sits at $310.3 billion, up 1.47 percent on the month, which is modest: there is no massive dry powder building.

The crowd sentiment gauge reads 74, firmly in Greed territory, near the top of its 30-day range of 25 to 74. Yet the tape contradicts this comfort. Price is down on the day across every major, momentum is rolling over while trend is still intact, and liquidations are skewing toward longs that were leveraged in assets with the highest funding rates and tightest skews. Flows are small and mixed. The ETF bid is real but ebbing. Whales are pulling coins cold, a sign of conviction among holders, but the amounts are small relative to the open interest in play. This is a market resting after a month-long rally, with every window showing different timing. The central tension is this: the regime (above 200-day) and the sentiment (74 Greed) say one thing; the momentum, the liquidation profile, and the funding skew say another.

Watch for a reclaim of the 200-day by Doge and ADA, which would signal regime unity. Watch Bitcoin funding flip positive, which would indicate shorts are no longer paying and crowding has reversed. Watch whether the 48-hour whale outflow persists into next week or reverses back onto exchanges, a tell for whether holders are taking profits or accumulating. If ETF net flows for Bitcoin on the next two sessions both turn negative or fall below the five-session average, the traditional-finance bid has stalled. The mood is Greed but the mechanics are neutral; any of those three conditions would sharpen the picture.
